what_was_wrong: The envelope calculation summed each clause's (call_peak - clause_peak) * clause_duration, which is a time integral valid ONLY if clauses execute sequentially. 87.7% of multi-clause exec calls are PIPELINES, whose clauses run CONCURRENTLY, so their durations overlap and the sum double-counts wall time. The headline 48.8% is therefore dominated by calls to which the calculation does not apply.

sequential_only.status: VALID; this is the only structure where a clause-granular limit can resize over time

corrected_headline: For the 12.3% of multi-clause calls that are sequential-only, a single call-level limit over-provisions by 10.6% of the resource-time envelope, not 48.8%. The overstatement is roughly fivefold.
pipe_pattern_reinterpreted: All 1018 heavy-plus-long-reader pairs are joined by a pipe, verified from clause_telemetry.command, e.g. 'apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq python3-pip 2>&1 | tail -5'. Because a pipeline is concurrent, the heavy command needs its memory for its own duration and the blocked reader adds NO additional hold. The claim in 2886683 that 6512 GB-seconds would be released by a clause-granular limit is WRONG. There is nothing to release: the memory is required for exactly as long as it is held.
what_survives: 48.4% of exec calls contain two or more timed clauses; tool calls are compositionally heterogeneous. Unchanged.
Clause-level resource demands within a call differ widely (peak/min dispersion). Unchanged as a descriptive fact about demands.
NEW and structurally important: 87.7% of multi-clause exec calls are pipelines. Agents overwhelmingly compose with | rather than &&, which is itself a workload characterization nobody has reported.
The blocked-reader phenomenon is real and verified; only its resource interpretation was wrong.
consequence_for_D1: Materially weakened. The mechanism can only recover over-provisioning where clauses are sequential, which is 12.3% of multi-clause calls, and there the waste is 10.6%. Combined with the cap-versus-reservation problem and the cgroup-v2 finding that lowering memory.max below usage triggers reclaim and then OOM kills, D1's remaining value is small enough that it should not be pursued on this evidence without a new argument.
how_it_was_caught: By checking whether the heavy and reader clauses overlap in time. The serialized clause records carry no timestamps and never populate in_pipe/in_loop/in_subst (0 of 13960), so an initial inference of 'sequential' from in_pipe=False was itself invalid. The structure was finally recovered from clause_telemetry.command.
